SK2071 The structured log template names the same property twice

A logging call's constant message template uses one property name for more than one hole, so the structured event cannot carry both values.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

The rendered line looks right, which is what makes this one survive review. The structured event is the part that is wrong: one key cannot hold two values, so a sink keeps one of them and the other is gone, and which one survives is the sink's business rather than the author's. The field a dashboard filters on is then silently either the first value or the last. ⚠ Nothing hosts this, for any logging framework. CA2017 counts holes against arguments, so logger.LogInformation("{X} then {X}", a, b) is arity-correct and it stays silent — measured in a probe project, at default analysis level and at AnalysisMode=All, rather than read from documentation. That is why this rule covers Microsoft.Extensions.Logging as well as Serilog, where SK2070 deliberately does not: the concept has no host anywhere, so ADR-008 has nothing to defer to. There is no fix, because the second property's name is the thing the author has to choose and no edit can choose it.

Example

Instead of:

logger.LogInformation("Moved {Path} to {Path}", from, to);

Write:

logger.LogInformation("Moved {From} to {To}", from, to);

When it does not fire

⚠ `{@Order}` and `{Order}` are the same property and are reported. Serilog's @ (destructure) and $ (stringify) sigils select how a value is captured, not what it is called; a parser that keeps the sigil sees two names where the logger sees one and misses the duplicate this rule exists to find. ⚠ Comparison is ordinal, so `{Count}` and `{count}` are two properties and neither is reported. They are two properties to every sink there is, so no value is lost and calling them a duplicate would be an opinion about naming dressed as a defect. ⚠ The finding is reported on the whole template argument rather than on the repeated name. A hole's offset is known within the template's value, and the value and the source spelling diverge at the first escape sequence — one \n earlier in the literal and a span computed from the value points one character short. A slightly coarse span that is always right beats a precise one that is quietly wrong inside a baseline fingerprint. ⚠ One finding per repeated name, not one per extra occurrence: a name written three times is one decision, and reporting it twice would report the same decision as many times as it was made. {{ and }} are escapes and are not holes. A positional template ("{0} {0}") withdraws the analysis, because indices are string.Format semantics rather than property names; CA2253 is the rule that says not to write one. A non-constant template is not analysed. Binding is by containing type (Serilog.ILogger, Serilog.Log, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions) and by the parameter each spells messageTemplate, message or messageFormat, never by method name, so a domain method called Information is not a logging call. Generated code is excluded.
